title: Finite-pushforward reduction of the tensor comparison
statement:
Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $S'$ be $K$-schemes and let $g:T\to S'$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism. Put $X'=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}S'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, with projections $p:X'\to X$, $f':X'\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$. Let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $K$, put $k=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $\pi:X_i\to X$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $\mathcal F$ be a $k$-module sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Write $M=\pi_*\underline{k}$, with constant sheaf as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Put $X'_i=X_i\times_X X'$, $Y_i=X'_i\times_{X'}Y$, and write $p_i:X'_i\to X_i$, $\pi':X'_i\to X'$, $\rho:Y_i\to Y$, $h_i:Y_i\to X'_i$, $f_i'=f'\pi'$ and $e_i=e\rho$ for the induced maps. Work in $D^+(-_{\mathrm{et}},k)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and direct and inverse images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Finite exchange, the finite projection formula, and derived direct-image composition give canonical isomorphisms
$$p^{-1}M\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\cong\pi'_* (f_i')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F,$$
$$Rh_*\bigl(h^{-1}p^{-1}M\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}e^{-1}\mathcal F\bigr)\cong\pi'_*Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F.$$
Under these isomorphisms the comparison adjoint to $1\otimes e^{-1}\varepsilon_g$ equals $\pi'_*$ of the untensored comparison $(f_i')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F\to Rh_{i,*}e_i^{-1}\mathcal F$ adjoint to $e_i^{-1}\varepsilon_g$. In particular invertibility of the latter implies invertibility of the former.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward diagram and calculation

proof.text: The two base changes $\pi'$ and $\rho$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a), and proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. Finite direct image is exact on abelian sheaves by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. On module sheaves, direct image has that underlying abelian functor [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; the faithful exact forgetful functor preserves kernels and cokernels [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](1), so the module direct image is exact too. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies $R\pi'_*=\pi'_*$ and $R\rho_*=\rho_*$ canonically on all complexes used below. No resolution-acyclicity assumption is added.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text: Finite exchange [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-exchange] for $(\pi,p)$ identifies $P:=p^{-1}M$ with $\pi'_*k_{X'_i}$. For $(\pi',h)$ it gives $E:h^{-1}\pi'_*k_{X'_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_*k_{Y_i}$. These are also module isomorphisms, by [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. Inverse image carries the constant coefficient sheaf to itself [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](1). Put $A=(f')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F$, $V=e^{-1}\mathcal F$, $B=(\pi')^{-1}A$, and $Q=\rho^{-1}V=e_i^{-1}\mathcal F$. All inverse-image composition identifications below use [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. The map $\delta=e^{-1}\varepsilon_g:h^{-1}A\to V$ pulls back to $\delta_i=\rho^{-1}\delta:h_i^{-1}B\to Q$, the counit map $e_i^{-1}\varepsilon_g$.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-0f0g] to finite proper $\pi'$, torsion ring $k$, first argument $k_{X'_i}$ and second argument $A$. With the tensor unit identification this gives $\phi_A:\pi'_*k_{X'_i}\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}A\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi'_*B$. Since $B=(f_i')^{-1}Rg_*\mathcal F$, composing with Step 2 gives precisely the first isomorphism of the item. We use the canonical projection arrow [def-kun-projection-formula-map], whose $(\pi')^{-1}\dashv R\pi'_*$-transpose is $\varepsilon_{\pi',k}\otimes1_B$, with the monoidal pullback identification [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] understood. The tensor unit contributes no higher Tor: its complex is the free rank-one coefficient module in degree zero.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text: Apply the same projection formula to $\rho$ and $V$. Together with $E$ it gives $\lambda_V:h^{-1}\pi'_*k_{X'_i}\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}V\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_*Q$. Its $\rho^{-1}\dashv R\rho_*$-transpose is $(\varepsilon_{\rho,k}\otimes1_Q)\circ(\rho^{-1}E\otimes1)$. The canonical composition isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], applied to $h\rho=\pi'h_i$ with constant coefficients, give $C:Rh_*\rho_*Q\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi'_*Rh_{i,*}Q$. Thus $\Psi=C\circ Rh_*\lambda_V$, preceded by Step 2, is the second isomorphism of the item.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text: We check equality of the maps, including the composition convention. The composition comparison in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] is the ordinary composite direct-image identification on a K-injective complex: every direct image here preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since its module inverse image is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Thus one may take the second K-injective resolution in that comparison to be the identity. The sheaf inverse/direct-image composition isomorphisms are module-linear and carry the composite unit to the ordinary unit [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. By the Hom bijection and counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], $C$ therefore identifies the two successive adjunction bijections for $(h,\rho)$ and $(\pi',h_i)$ with the same bijection for the composite map $Y_i\to X'$. This also follows directly by applying the two termwise Hom bijections on the chosen K-injective representative, so it requires no further base-change theorem.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text:
Write $\alpha:P\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}A\to Rh_*(h^{-1}P\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}V)$ for the comparison, and $\beta:B\to Rh_{i,*}Q$ for the untensored comparison. Use $P=\pi'_*k_{X'_i}$ as in Step 2. To prove $\Psi\alpha=\pi'_*(\beta)\phi_A$, use the common composite adjunction of Step 5. By definition the $h$-transpose of $\alpha$ is $1_{h^{-1}P}\otimes\delta$. Naturality of the Hom bijection in its target says that the further $\rho$-transpose of $Rh_*\lambda_V\circ\alpha$ is the $\rho$-transpose of $\lambda_V$ followed after $\rho^{-1}(1\otimes\delta)$. Expanding that transpose by [def-kun-projection-formula-map] yields, on $Y_i$,
$$s=\bigl(\varepsilon_{\rho,k}\circ\rho^{-1}E\bigr)\otimes\rho^{-1}\delta.$$
The source is $\rho^{-1}h^{-1}P\otimes_k^{\mathbf L}\rho^{-1}h^{-1}A$ and the target is $Q$. Bifunctorial monoidality of inverse image is [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal].

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text:
Now transpose $\pi'_*(\beta)\phi_A$ first under $(\pi')^{-1}\dashv\pi'_*$ and then under $h_i^{-1}\dashv Rh_{i,*}$. Naturality of the first Hom bijection gives $\beta$ after the transpose $\varepsilon_{\pi',k}\otimes1_B$ of $\phi_A$. The second gives $\delta_i$ after its inverse image. Consequently this route is
$$t= h_i^{-1}(\varepsilon_{\pi',k})\otimes\rho^{-1}\delta.$$
The source and target are exactly those of $s$ after the cartesian inverse-image identification. The mate definition of finite exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] gives
$$\varepsilon_{\rho,k}\circ\rho^{-1}E=h_i^{-1}(\varepsilon_{\pi',k}).$$
This is its defining adjunct identity, on the degree-zero constant sheaf; the equality is module-linear because the underlying unit and counit are those of the module adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact](3). Hence $s=t$. Injectivity of the composite Hom bijection proves the required equality of the canonical maps, rather than merely an isomorphism between their objects.

source.place: Tag 0F1J, lemma-punctual-base-change-upgrade, final finite-pushforward calculation; Tags 0959 (finite exchange), 03QP (finite exactness), 0F0G (projection formula)

proof.text: If $\beta$ is invertible, $\pi'_*(\beta)$ has inverse $\pi'_*(\beta^{-1})$. Since $\phi_A$ and $\Psi$ are isomorphisms, the equality of Steps 6--7 gives $\alpha=\Psi^{-1}\pi'_*(\beta)\phi_A$, which is invertible. This proves the last clause without assuming the untensored comparison theorem as an additional dependency.
